aesthetic.name: Seed Packet
aesthetic.influences: 1930s–50s seed packets, mail-order nursery catalogues, rubber date stamps, botanical engravings, perforated coupons
aesthetic.summary: A brand dressed as a vintage seed packet: kraft paper, stamped labels and a tear-off strip.
aesthetic.coreTrick: Every surface is a printed paper packet: kraft stock, a rubber-stamped ink label, and a perforated tear line where a card meets its footer.
aesthetic.motto: Sow by the date stamped on the back.

fonts.why: Wood type and slab headlines are what packet printers had in the case; a typewriter body reads like the growing notes on the back.

build.surface: Kraft paper with a double ink frame, a perforated tear line and rubber-stamped ink; no shadows.
build.pressText: Rest: a flat printed ink with an inner keyline. Hover: the fill flips to full ink with canvas text. Pressed: the stamp sinks 2px, as if pushed into the pad.
build.icons: Square-ended 2px ink strokes in caps-height glyphs, drawn like woodcut marks; a selected icon is filled solid ink.
build.appIcon: A kraft tile with a double ink frame and a single sprouting seedling in one flat green ink, a row of perforation holes along the bottom edge.

motto.label: Motto
motto.text: Sow by the date stamped on the back.

canvas.use: Page and panel background, tinted slightly toward the primary hue

ink.use: Headlines, body text, borders, hover fill
ink.never: Large background fields in light mode

primary.use: The one main action per view; selected state
primary.never: Body text; more than one CTA per view

secondary.use: Secondary buttons, chips, second data series

accent.use: One spark per view: the highlighted headline word, new badges
accent.never: Buttons, body text, borders, large fills

do: Print every surface flat: one ink border weight, no gradients, no blur.
End a section with a perforation or a stamp, never a plain gap.
dont: Use glossy, glass or soft shadows: nothing here is lit, it is printed.

params.text: Lot 14 · 2027 season · Tear off and keep

hero.alt: A botanical engraving of a sprouting seed: a husk under hatched soil, roots below, a stem with two leaves and a bud, in ink line work with one flat green ink, framed like a packet front.

notes.text: The core trick is not on the board yet. Nothing reads as a seed packet: no perforated tear line, no rubber-stamped label. The hero should feel like the front of a packet: a stamped lot label near the headline and a perforated tear strip across the bottom of the hero.

The art is the generic circle-and-shapes placeholder. Replace it with a botanical engraving: a sprouting seed or a seedling drawn in ink line work, printed in one or two flat inks like an old packet illustration.

Buttons are still a generic blue slab with a hard border. They should look rubber-stamped: an ink outline with a slightly worn edge on kraft, caps text, and the fill as a flat printed ink, not a screen-blue panel.

rounds.summary: Square corners everywhere; palette chips need to read as printed swatches.

notes.text: Palette chips are plain screen tiles. Print them as colour swatches the way a packet shows the flower colour: square chips with a printed caption and a thin ink keyline.

rounds.summary: The packet now reads on the board: a botanical engraving, a stamped lot label, perforated tear lines and stamped-ink buttons on kraft.
changes: art.hero: generic circle-and-shapes placeholder replaced by a framed botanical engraving of a sprouting seed, ink line work with one flat green ink
new moves in js/moves/printed-stock.js: tear-line, stamped-label, ink-stamp, tear-edge (generic, with params)
added board moves stamped-label (hero kicker as a tilted, worn rubber stamp) and tear-line (perforated line under the hero and above the footer, captioned Tear here)
kit.button-primary: hard-offset - ink-stamp (dulled flat ink, inner keyline, caps text, speckled wear); ink-stamp also listed in moves because its text-contrast tokens only run from there
kit.card and kit.modal: hard-offset - tear-edge (ink frame with a perforated strip along the bottom)
layout.palette: swatches - chips with palette-board-form (square chips with a keyline and a caps caption)

variants.change: art: placeholder shapes - botanical engraving svg
structure: added tear-line on hero and footer, plus tear-edge on card and modal

notes.text: On the deck cover the hero tear line and the footer tear line sit next to each other and the footer text crowds them. Use where "hero" only or give the footer room.
Leftover template text: meta.fonts.why, build.pressText, build.icons, build.appIcon and rules.do/dont still hold placeholder sentences. Write them for this look.
The speckle wear on stamped buttons is even and reads as noise at small sizes; try fewer, larger flecks along the edge only.

rounds.summary: Kraft holds in dark mode now; rules and font note rewritten; wider label tracking kept. Palette chip and deck foot need work.
changes: colour recipe warm-paper-canvas: warmDark off → on
colour recipe warm-paper-canvas: cream #c8a46e → light #c8a46e / dark #c8a46e
colour recipe warm-paper-canvas: cream dark #c8a46e → #3a2a19
why these fonts: One sentence on why these font classes carry the look (stag… → Wood type and slab headlines are what packet printers had i…
do rules: Keep one border weight everywhere. → Print every surface flat: one ink border weight, no gradien…
don't rules: Use blur shadows. → Use glossy, glass or soft shadows: nothing here is lit, it…
do rules: Print every surface flat: one ink border weight, no gradien… → Print every surface flat: one ink border weight, no gradien…

notes.text: The canvas chip disappears: it is the page colour with no edge, in light and dark. Every chip should be a printed swatch with an ink keyline so the canvas one still reads.

The striped blue band with a circle at the foot of the cover comes from another look and fights the kraft. Make the foot a tear-off coupon instead: a perforated strip with the lot number and season, printed in ink on kraft.

rounds.summary: One tear line on the cover with room below it, a printed coupon foot in place of the striped band, keylined palette chips, fewer larger edge flecks on stamped buttons, and the leftover template text written.
changes: tear-line: new gap param (default 0); the spec uses where hero only with gap 14, so the footer text no longer crowds a second line (n5)
new move coupon-foot in js/moves/printed-marks.js: on the deck cover it hides the pattern band and prints a perforated tear-off coupon strip reading 'Lot 14 · 2027 season · Tear off and keep' (n9)
new move swatch-keyline in js/moves/printed-marks.js: every palette chip gets a 2px ink keyline, so the canvas chip reads in light and dark (n8)
ink-stamp: new params wearAt (all|edge, default all) and fleck; the spec uses wearAt edge, wear 0.4, fleck 1.6: six larger flecks just inside the keyline instead of even speckle (n7)
build.pressText, build.icons and build.appIcon rewritten for the kraft and stamp look; fonts.why and rules were already rewritten in round 4 (n6)

variants.change: structure: tear-line where both - hero, with gap
structure: deck cover foot band - coupon-foot
material (button-primary): ink-stamp wear - edge flecks (fleck 2.2 killed as too big, 1.6 applied)

notes.text: On the small Rest/Pressed buttons an edge fleck can land beside the label; consider fewer flecks when the button is under 120px wide.
The cover band is hidden by CSS from coupon-foot because an imported style cannot set deck.coverBand false; the coupon holds one text line only (lot and season), no split stub.
